Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

salary noun

also salaries, monthly salary, annual salary

classical

Tac. Agr. 42.2: salārium tamen prōcōnsulāre solitum offerrī
Suet. Tib. 46: numquam salāriō, cibāriīs tantum sustentāvit
Plin. Ep. 4.12.2: ante lēgitimum salāriī tempus
M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages

salārium, salāriī n.

noun, second declension

a salary, fixed pay

In imperial prose the fixed pay of officials and of the emperor’s companions (Lewis & Short); the source of the English word. Pliny says it was named from salt (NH 31.89, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • mercēs, mercēdis f. — pay, wages; a fee

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 373: aequam mercēdem alicui solvere, to pay someone a fair salary; M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages

    Pay for work of any kind (see wage); Traupman’s word for a salary.

  • stīpendium, stīpendiī n. — pay; properly a soldier’s pay

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Liv. 1.20.3: stīpendium dē pūblicō statuit, (Numa) gave (the Vestals) a salary from public funds; M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages

    The soldier’s pay (Caes., Liv.), and so any regular stipend (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Pecūniae parcus ac tenāx comitēs peregrīnātiōnum expedītiōnumque numquam salāriō, cibāriīs tantum sustentāvit

    Sparing and close with money, he never kept the companions of his travels and campaigns on a salary, only on their foodSuet. Tib. 46

  • Salārium tamen prōcōnsulāre solitum offerrī et quibusdam ā sē ipsō concessum Agricolae nōn dedit

    But the salary of a proconsul, which was usually offered, and which he had himself granted to some, he did not give AgricolaTac. Agr. 42.2

See also wage, income, employee, employer, pension, earn.

SourcesLewis & Short: salarium · Lewis & Short: salarius · Lewis & Short: merces · Lewis & Short: stipendium

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages.
